answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it may submit bids, then slash that bond when a fraud challenge proves the account fabricated trades or identities. The bond does not prove a person is unique; it makes mass identities costly and gives honest participants a reason to report them. An attacker hoping to dominate an orchard marketplace must tie up capital in every fake account and risks losing it, even if each account uses a different cipher or claims to come from a separate island.
